name: View modifier
first: A method of a view that returns a new view, which holds the original view and one change to it, such as space around it.

dependsOn.why: A modifier is called on a view, and returns a view.
dependsOn.whyInExample: `city` is a `Text`, a view, and `padding(8)` returns a new view that holds it.

what.is: A view modifier is a method that every view has, such as `padding(8)` or `opacity(0.5)`. It does not change the view it is called on. It returns a new view that holds that view and the change.
what.afterExample: Lines 6 to 8 print the type of each view. `padded` is a new view that holds `city`, and `faded` is a new view that holds `padded`.
what.problem: Views need many small changes, such as space around them, a color, or a size. A modifier adds one change at a time to any view, so no new type of view is needed for each mix of changes.
what.how: Each modifier returns a new view, of a type that SwiftUI calls modified content, which holds the view it was called on and the change. Calling several modifiers in a row puts each new view around the one before, so the order of the calls is the order of the nesting.

when.text: Use modifiers to change how a view looks or behaves, in the order the changes should happen. Space added before a background is inside the background, and space added after it is outside.
Don't expect a modifier to change the view in a variable. `city` is still a plain `Text` after line 4: the change is in the new view, `padded`.

parts.name: The modifier calls, lines 4 and 5
parts.text: Line 4 calls `padding(8)` on `city`, which returns a new view with 8 points of space around `city`. Line 5 calls `opacity(0.5)` on that new view, which returns another view that draws it half transparent. Neither call changes the view it is called on.

steps.text: Line 3 makes a `Text` that shows `"Lima"`, and stores it in `city`.
Line 4 calls `padding(8)` on `city`. It returns a new view that holds `city` and the padding, and line 4 stores it in `padded`.
Line 5 calls `opacity(0.5)` on `padded`, and stores the new view, which holds `padded`, in `faded`.
Line 6 prints the type of `city`, which is still {{Text}}.
Line 7 prints the type of `padded`: {{ModifiedContent<Text, _PaddingLayout>}}. It holds a `Text` and the padding.
Line 8 prints the type of `faded`, which holds the type of `padded` inside it: {{ModifiedContent<ModifiedContent<Text, _PaddingLayout>, _OpacityEffect>}}.

end.text: A modifier returns a new view around the view it is called on. Each modifier in a row adds one more layer, in the order they are written.
